svg.title: connpool: how a connection flows
svg.desc: Animated diagram: idle reuse with health check, release as a fresh copy, discard of an unfit connection, dialing with a dial token then a slot, and the maintainIdle worker.
svg.text: open conns ≤ MaxPoolSize (slots) · concurrent dials ≤ MaxConcurrency (dialTokens) · this loop: MaxPoolSize = 4, MaxConcurrency = 2
refillChan nudge · ticker: evict expired idle conns · fill to MinIdle

g.text: acquireIdle takes the oldest idle conn without blocking. reusable() clears deadlines and peeks the socket
(non-blocking recv MSG_PEEK on Unix) before the conn is handed over.
2 · conn.Close() returns it to the pool
After the same health check, release puts a fresh *Conn copy into idleChan. The caller's old handle stays
released and returns net.ErrClosed forever, even after the socket is lent out again.
3 · An unfit idle conn is discarded
The peek sees EOF (peer closed) or the conn outlived its lifespan / IdleTimeout: closeConn closes it, frees its
slot and nudges refillChan. Acquire gets errConnDiscarded and simply tries the next idle conn.
4 · No idle conn: dial a new one
Within AcquireTimeout, take a dial token first, then a slot (never the reverse, which could deadlock).
openConnection dials with capped exponential backoff; the token is returned once the dial is done.
Both conns are released. With MinIdle > 0, maintainIdle evicts expired idle conns on its ticker and dials
more to keep MinIdle ready. Pool Close() closes idle conns; checked-out ones close on release.
